name: Tessera Industries Signal Cloaking Device SCD-1
product_name: Tessera Industries Signal Cloaking Device SCD-1
description: A pocket-sized device that masks the electromagnetic emissions of the wearer's neural interface and all electronic devices within a 1-meter radius. The SCD-1 does not jam signals — it absorbs and contains them using a metamaterial shell, preventing any EM leakage that could be detected by passive surveillance. The device makes the wearer electronically invisible without disrupting their own device functionality — they can still use their neural interface and devices normally, but no emissions escape the containment field.
story_hooks: An SCD-1 user walked through a total surveillance zone without triggering a single sensor — the only evidence of their passage was a person-shaped absence in the electromagnetic background.
A modified SCD-1 with expanded radius has been deployed in a meeting room, creating a permanently EM-silent space where no electronic surveillance can operate.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek cylindrical device resembling a premium vape pen or compact medical injector. The form is deliberately innocuous—designed to blend into everyday carry. The metamaterial shell creates an iridescent, oil-slick surface that seems to shift color depending on viewing angle, hinting at its EM-absorbing properties without advertising function.
physical_description.dimensions: 12 cm tall, 2.5 cm diameter—fits easily in a shirt pocket or jacket sleeve
physical_description.weight_description: Negligibly light (100g)—pocketable without noticeable burden, easily carried as daily wear
physical_description.primary_material: Metamaterial composite shell (proprietary Vasquez Biocompatible substrate) over a titanium-aluminum alloy skeleton
physical_description.finish: Matte with microscopic lattice texture visible under close inspection; surface has an uncanny quality—light seems to be absorbed rather than reflected. No visible seams or ventilation ports.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with oil-slick iridescence (purples, teals, sickly greens) that shifts in low light. Minimal accent lighting: a single dim amber LED ring near the base that pulses during active containment.
physical_description.interface_elements: Recessed capacitive touch panel on the upper third (unlock/activate); subtle haptic feedback system (no clicking). Micro-USB charging port recessed flush with the body. Status indicator: amber pulse = active, green steady = standby, red flash = low battery. No screen—entirely haptic interface.
distinctive_features: Metamaterial shell exhibits visible light-absorption distortion—surrounding environment appears slightly warped when viewing the device directly
Microscopic chevron patterns etched into the surface, barely visible but create a sense of engineered complexity
The amber LED pulses in a rhythm that mimics a heartbeat—psychological reinforcement of 'living' invisibility
Cooling fins are internal; exterior appears perfectly smooth but slightly warm to touch during operation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Embossed Φ symbol (QUANTA payment currency) and 'TESSERA INDUSTRIES' in minimalist sans-serif on the base. Tiny Vasquez Biocompatible Materials logo (stylized helix) laser-etched near the charging port. Regulatory stamps for GLMZ compliance discreetly applied to the underside.
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use, the device is warm (not hot) and the amber LED pulses steadily. The iridescent finish appears to 'drink' light from surrounding sources. Micro-condensation may form on the surface in humid conditions due to passive thermal management of the EM absorption process. User's neural interface HUD shows a persistent 'CLOAKED' indicator while active.
